design_detail: Laboratory chemical screening of seven commercial oral products for 43 compounds, funded and designed by the maker of two of them (see funding): two variants of the maker's tobacco-free pouch brand (ZYN dry and moist), one Swedish snus (General) made by the same company, two moist snuffs (a reference product and a US pouched product), and two nicotine replacement products (a lozenge and a gum). One batch of each product, triplicate analyses, results per gram of wet weight. Most analyses were done at an external accredited laboratory, some in the company's own laboratory. The schema has no design for a laboratory analysis of products; 'in-vitro' is the nearest. No people, no nicotine uptake and no health outcome were measured.
can_establish: What the maker-funded screening found above its quantification limits, per gram of product, in these seven products; that for the two ZYN variants none of ten nitrosamines and none of seven polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons was above the limits used, while a few other constituents (formaldehyde, chromium, ammonia and, in one variant, nickel) were; and how the number and level of quantified constituents compared across the pouch, snus, moist snuff and replacement products in the same programme.
cannot_establish: Anything about tobacco-free nicotine pouches as a category (two variants of one brand, one batch each); that nitrosamines are absent (the limit for the four tobacco-specific ones was 0.01 microgram per gram, which the AI reader works out as roughly 4 to 8 ng in a ZYN pouch, roughly ten times or more above the limit in the independent German analysis); what people take in or whether any product is harmless or less harmful than another (no uptake, biomarker or health outcome was measured, and the Discussion's 'low toxicity' is an inference from content); that snus or moist snuff in general resemble the single products tested; or what an independent laboratory would find in the same products.

sample.recruitment: Products, not people. The two ZYN products and the snus came from the maker's own distribution centre in Stockholm; the replacement products from online pharmacies in Sweden; the moist snuff reference product from a university tobacco laboratory in North Carolina; the pouched moist snuff from a wholesaler in Kentucky (Material and methods › Sample handling and analysis, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Compounds chosen by the maker: 36 on the US Food and Drug Administration's list of harmful and potentially harmful constituents, four for the maker's own snus standard and two more nitrosamines to cover the four tobacco-specific ones (Material and methods › Selected compounds, 1st paragraph). Agrochemicals covered by the standard were left out as beyond scope (2nd paragraph).
sample.attrition: None described. Where one or two of three replicates were below the quantification limit they were set to half the limit for the mean and standard deviation; polonium-210 was a single measurement.
sample.selection_effects: One batch of each product, chosen by the funder, with its own pouch and snus samples supplied from its distribution centre rather than bought at retail; one flavour per pouch variant; one product per comparison category. The date of analysis is not stated (analyses were done within 3 weeks of obtaining each product; the references were accessed in March to June 2021). The authors say no chemical data on ZYN had been published.

exposure.measurement: Mostly an external laboratory accredited to ISO 17025 (Eurofins, Lidköping): metals by ICP-MS; nitrosamines (NNN, NNK, NAT, NAB, NDMA) by HPLC with tandem mass spectrometry; polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons by GC-MS or HPLC with fluorescence; aldehydes, nitrite, ammonia, aflatoxins, ochratoxin A, coumarin, ethyl carbamate, total nicotine and pH by standard or in-house methods. Done in the maker's own laboratory: uranium-235 and -238, five more nitrosamines (NDELA, NMOR, NPIP, NPYR, NSAR), anabasine and nornicotine, and the calculation of unprotonated nicotine from pH. Polonium-210 at a Canadian laboratory. For the replacement products the methods were validated but not accredited. Triplicate analyses of the whole product including the pouch (Material and methods › Sample handling and analysis, 2nd paragraph; Table 2). Quantification limits for the four tobacco-specific nitrosamines 0.01 microgram per gram; NDMA 0.20 ng per gram; other nitrosamines 10 to 25 ng per gram; benzo[a]pyrene 1 ng per gram; other polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons 30 ng per gram (Tables 3 and 4).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Measured product content, not a dose: total nicotine in mg per gram wet weight (Table 6): ZYN dry 7.63, ZYN moist 12.00, replacement lozenge 3.20, replacement gum 1.30, snus 8.13, loose moist snuff 9.97, pouched moist snuff 8.47; unprotonated nicotine 4.87, 7.87, 2.57, 1.28, 7.11, 3.23 and 3.65; pH 8.3, 8.3, 8.6, 9.9, 8.9, 7.7 and 7.9; product mass 0.4, 0.8, 0.6, 1.2, 1.0 (loose not given) and 1.3 g (Table 1). Content per pouch is not printed; multiplying gives about 3 mg for ZYN dry and 10 mg for ZYN moist against 8 mg for the snus pouch (AI reader's arithmetic). Oral use; no use was studied.
exposure.polysubstance: Not applicable (products). Forty-three compounds screened; those below the limit of quantification are not reported as zero.

comparison.controls: Within the study: one Swedish snus, two moist snuffs and two nicotine replacement products, analysed by the same programme. No cigarette was analysed; no other pouch brand was analysed.
comparison.matching: Per gram of wet weight, so products of different mass (0.4 to 1.3 g) are not compared per unit of use; moisture ranges from 3% to 53%.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Not applicable to a product analysis; what was not measured: other pouch brands, other batches, product ageing, nicotine uptake, flavour compounds, and agrochemicals.

outcomes.instruments: Concentrations above the quantification limit, mean and standard deviation of triplicates, in Tables 3 to 6; counts of compounds quantified per product.
outcomes.validity_norms: Methods are described in Table 2 with validation and accreditation status in the text; recoveries, blanks and uncertainty are not given in the main text. No thresholds or safety limits are applied.
outcomes.operationalization: Harm is not measured; 'low toxicity' is inferred from the number and level of quantified constituents (Discussion, 5th paragraph).

analysis.effect_sizes: No effect sizes. Nitrosamines: none of ten above the limits in either ZYN variant or either replacement product; snus NNN 0.44, NNK 0.19, NAT 0.31 and NAB 0.02 microgram per gram and NDMA 0.24 ng per gram; loose moist snuff NNN 3.63, NNK 2.27; pouched moist snuff NNN 2.53, NNK 0.92 microgram per gram, so five to 12 times the snus levels (Table 3). Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons: none in ZYN, replacement products or snus; six of seven in loose moist snuff and five in pouched, benzo[a]pyrene 113 and 74 ng per gram (Table 4). Other constituents (microgram per gram unless stated): ZYN dry formaldehyde 10.3, chromium 0.160, ammonia 62, nickel 0.067; ZYN moist formaldehyde 1.5, chromium 0.099, ammonia 66; replacement lozenge nickel 0.086; replacement gum cadmium 0.043, chromium 0.850, lead 0.067, nickel 0.243, acetaldehyde 4.7, ammonia 4.5, uranium-235 0.14 and uranium-238 2.76 Bq per kg; snus arsenic 0.062, cadmium 0.270, chromium 0.523, lead 0.177, nickel 0.817, selenium 0.088, acetaldehyde 10.0, ammonia 847, formaldehyde 1.6, anabasine 28.5, nornicotine 162, ochratoxin A 0.86 ng per gram and polonium-210 5.4 Bq per kg (Tables 5 and 6). Compounds quantified, nicotine included: replacement lozenge 2, ZYN moist 4, ZYN dry 5, replacement gum 9, snus 19, pouched moist snuff 26, loose moist snuff 27 (Discussion, 3rd paragraph).
analysis.preregistration_detail: No protocol or registration is mentioned (a laboratory screening).
analysis.selective_reporting: All 43 compounds are in Tables 3 to 6. The maker chose the compounds, the products and the comparison categories; agrochemicals were left out. Data are said to be available on request; recoveries, blanks and uncertainty were not in the text read.
analysis.power: Not applicable (no tests). One batch per product, triplicate analyses.

interpretation_gap.results_show: In one batch each of two ZYN variants, none of ten nitrosamines and none of seven polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons was above the quantification limits (0.01 microgram per gram for the four tobacco-specific nitrosamines; 30 ng per gram for most polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons); formaldehyde, chromium and ammonia were quantified in both and nickel in the dry variant; four or five compounds in all, against two or nine in the replacement products and 19 in the snus and 26 or 27 in the moist snuffs. Moist snuff held five to 12 times the nitrosamines of the snus. Nothing was measured in people.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Abstract: tobacco-free pouches 'may serve as a low-risk alternative' to cigarettes and to snus and moist snuff; the two ZYN products 'contained no nitrosamines or' polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; the number of quantified constituents was similar for ZYN and replacement products and found at low levels. Discussion: few constituents at low levels 'suggesting that the products have a low toxicity'; the results 'confirm' a manufacturer's earlier study; clinical data suggest 'a lower abuse liability' than cigarettes. Gaps: (1) the low-risk and low-toxicity statements are inferences; neither risk nor toxicity was measured, and the paper itself says a full risk assessment needs more data; (2) 'no nitrosamines' means none above limits of about 4 to 8 ng per ZYN pouch for the tobacco-specific ones, and an independent German laboratory with a limit roughly ten times or more lower found traces in 26 of 44 other pouch products (see sc_mallock_2024); the two do not conflict, but the abstract's wording does not carry the limit; (3) the results are for two variants of one maker's brand, yet the title and abstract speak of 'novel nicotine pouch products'; (4) the Background's 'convincingly shown' lower harm of snus than smoking cites one review, which was itself supported by the same company (see sc_lee_2013); (5) the Discussion's inferences on uptake and abuse liability rest on other studies whose funders are not stated here and were not read. In the authors' favour, they state that the data are limited to constituent content and that long-term epidemiological data are needed.

timeline.event: Azzopardi et al.: a similar screening of 26 compounds in a pouch brand, a Swedish-type snus, a moist snuff and replacement products, which this paper says it confirms; the German paper in this batch describes the study as by a manufacturer and its quantification limit as much less sensitive than its own (as described; not read).

Independent German laboratory analysis of 46 pouch products from 20 producers: nicotine 1.79 to 47.5 mg per pouch; tobacco-specific nitrosamines detected at trace levels in 26 of 44 nicotine pouches with a limit of quantification roughly ten times or more lower than this paper's (AI reader's arithmetic); funded by a federal risk-assessment institute; no company funding declared.

Scoping review of pouch studies that splits findings by industry and non-industry funding. It does not cite this paper or the German analysis above, but reports other content analyses (70 US tobacco-free products, 50 pouches, 31 pouches sold in Germany).

Systematic review of snus and pouches that cites this paper as showing similar numbers of constituents in pouches and replacement products, noting only that the pouches came from one manufacturer; it does not say that manufacturer funded the study.

replication.where_it_stands: A single maker-funded laboratory comparison of two ZYN variants with a snus, two moist snuffs and two replacement products. It has not been re-run on the same products by an independent laboratory, and the independent German analysis of other products used a more sensitive nitrosamine method and found traces. Read as what these seven products held, per gram, at the stated limits.

funding.funder: Swedish Match AB, which markets the ZYN and General products described (as printed).
funding.declared_conflicts: All authors are employees of or otherwise funded by Swedish Match AB (as printed). The funding statement says the funder designed the study, interpreted the data and wrote the manuscript, and that analyses and data collection were mainly (the wording adds 'if possible') done at external laboratories.
funding.affiliations_note: All four authors are in Regulatory & Scientific Affairs, Swedish Match AB, Stockholm. The company's own laboratory did part of the analysis (Table 2). The Background cites one review for the statement that long-term studies have 'convincingly shown' lower harm from snus than from smoking, which is a review supported by the same company (see sc_lee_2013). Recorded as a flag for closer reading, not as a reason to discount the measurements: most were made at an accredited external laboratory and are tabulated in full, and the claim sets this paper beside the independent German analysis.

what_would_settle_it: Independent, replicated analysis (several batches and brands, blanks and spiked controls, sensitive nitrosamine methods with limits per pouch reported) of pouches beside snus, moist snuff and nicotine replacement products in one laboratory, repeated over time; with measurements in people who use each product (nicotine uptake and urine or blood markers of nicotine, nitrosamines and metals) beside people who smoke and people who use no nicotine; and, for health, cohorts followed for years.

domains.domain: Products tested and how they were chosen
domains.note: Two variants of one maker's pouch brand, one snus, two moist snuffs and two replacement products, one batch each, the maker's own samples supplied from its distribution centre; chosen by the funder.

domains.domain: Independence of design, analysis and interpretation
domains.note: The funder designed the study, interpreted the data and wrote the manuscript; all four authors are its employees or funded by it; part of the analysis was done in its own laboratory.

Mostly an accredited external laboratory, triplicate analyses and limits printed for every compound; replacement-product methods not accredited; polonium a single measurement; recoveries and blanks not in the main text; nitrosamine limit roughly ten times or more above that of the independent German analysis (AI reader's arithmetic).
The same laboratories and methods for all seven products allow a like-for-like comparison, but there is one product per category, per gram of wet weight, and no cigarette.

'No nitrosamines' is a finding of 'below a quantification limit'; low toxicity and low risk are inferred from content; the text says 38 of 43 compounds were below the limit in both ZYN variants (true for the dry variant; 39 for the moist) and that ZYN dry formaldehyde was about five times snus (Table 6 gives 6.4 times).

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated risk-of-bias instrument exists for a laboratory analysis of commercial products (METHODS 5.3), so the editors' checklist is used with domains adapted to this design; the overall judgment cannot be less severe than the worst domain. The measurements come largely from an accredited external laboratory and are tabulated in full, so they can be read as what these seven products held per gram at the stated limits; the choice of products, the design and the interpretation sit with the maker. Citable for that content and for the comparison of those products; not for tobacco-free pouches as a category, for the absence of nitrosamines below the stated limits, or for any statement about uptake, toxicity or health.

key_findings.finding: Design and sources: seven oral products screened for 43 compounds, one batch each, triplicate analyses on the whole product, results per gram of wet weight; the two ZYN variants and the snus came from the maker's distribution centre. Most analyses at an external laboratory accredited to ISO 17025, some in the maker's laboratory; replacement-product methods validated but not accredited.
key_findings.locator: Material and methods › Tested products; Sample handling and analysis, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Table 2

key_findings.finding: Nitrosamines: none of ten above the quantification limit in either ZYN variant or either replacement product (limits 0.01 microgram per gram for NNN, NNK, NAT and NAB). Snus held NNN 0.44 and NNK 0.19 microgram per gram; loose moist snuff 3.63 and 2.27; pouched moist snuff 2.53 and 0.92, five to 12 times the snus.
key_findings.note: Below the limit does not mean absent; limit equals roughly 4 to 8 ng per ZYN pouch (AI reader's arithmetic from Table 1 masses).

key_findings.finding: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons: none above the limits in ZYN, replacement products or snus; six of seven in loose moist snuff and five in pouched moist snuff, benzo[a]pyrene 113 and 74 ng per gram.

Other constituents in ZYN: formaldehyde (10.3 microgram per gram in the dry variant, 1.5 in the moist), chromium (0.160 and 0.099), ammonia (62 and 66) and, in the dry variant only, nickel (0.067). Snus held formaldehyde 1.6, chromium 0.523, nickel 0.817, ammonia 847; the replacement gum held chromium 0.850, nickel 0.243, cadmium, lead, acetaldehyde, ammonia and uranium isotopes, and the lozenge only nickel (0.086).
key_findings.note: ZYN dry formaldehyde was the highest of all seven products.

key_findings.finding: Counts of compounds quantified, nicotine included, of 43: replacement lozenge 2, ZYN moist 4, ZYN dry 5, replacement gum 9, snus 19, pouched moist snuff 26, loose moist snuff 27. Snus held five nitrosamines, six metals, acetaldehyde, ammonia, anabasine, formaldehyde, nornicotine, ochratoxin A and polonium-210.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 3rd and 4th paragraphs; Results, 7th and 8th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Nicotine: total nicotine per gram was 7.63 (ZYN dry), 12.00 (ZYN moist), 3.20 (lozenge), 1.30 (gum), 8.13 (snus), 9.97 (loose moist snuff) and 8.47 mg (pouched moist snuff); unprotonated nicotine and pH are in Table 6 and Table 1. The authors say unprotonated nicotine does not capture how much is extracted in use, and that nicotine uptake needs clinical studies.
key_findings.locator: Results, 2nd paragraph; Tables 1 and 6; Discussion, 6th paragraph

key_findings.finding: Authors' reading: few constituents at low levels in ZYN 'suggesting that the products have a low toxicity'; consistent with in vitro studies they cite; the data are limited to constituent content, and long-term epidemiological data are needed for a full risk assessment. They say their results confirm a manufacturer's similar study in which no tobacco-specific nitrosamines or benzo[a]pyrene could be quantified in a pouch or replacement products.

Framing: the Background states that long-term studies have 'convincingly shown' snus to carry substantially fewer adverse effects than smoking (citing one review), describes the 'Swedish Experience' and the US Food and Drug Administration's 2019 modified-risk order for eight snus products including General, and says tobacco-free pouches 'should, at least in theory' not expose people to nitrosamines.
key_findings.note: Context and hypothesis, not a result of this study.

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says the two ZYN products 'contained no nitrosamines or' polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and the Conclusions say none were 'found'. The finding is none above quantification limits of 0.01 microgram per gram for NNN, NNK, NAT and NAB (about 4 to 8 ng per pouch given the masses in Table 1), 10 to 25 ng per gram for other nitrosamines and 30 ng per gram for most polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Abstract; Conclusions; Tables 3 and 4
reporting_issues.consequence: Absence below a limit; an independent laboratory with a much lower limit found traces in many other pouch products (see sc_mallock_2024).

reporting_issues.issue: Results say 38 of the 43 compounds were below the limit in 'the two types' of ZYN; that holds for the dry variant (five quantified) but the moist variant had four quantified (39 below). The abstract lists nickel among both products' findings; it was quantified only in the dry variant. The text says ZYN dry formaldehyde was about five times snus; Table 6 gives 10.3 against 1.6 microgram per gram, 6.4 times.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Abstract; Results, 3rd and 5th paragraphs; Discussion, 3rd paragraph; Table 6

reporting_issues.issue: The title and abstract speak of 'novel nicotine pouch products' and the Discussion infers 'low toxicity', but two variants of one brand were tested, one batch each, and no toxicity, uptake or health outcome was measured.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Title; Abstract; Discussion, 5th paragraph
reporting_issues.consequence: The results describe these samples; they cannot stand for pouches in general or for risk.

reporting_issues.issue: The funding statement says the analyses and collection of data were mainly 'if possible' carried out at external laboratories; Table 2 shows that analyses of five nitrosamines, two uranium isotopes, anabasine, nornicotine and unprotonated nicotine were done in the company's own laboratory.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML, Funding; Material and methods › Sample handling and analysis, 2nd paragraph; Table 2
reporting_issues.consequence: Which constituents were measured in-house is recoverable only from Table 2.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion supports 'lower abuse liability' and in vitro findings with other studies (its references 17 to 19, 21 to 23 and 25 to 29) without stating who funded them.
reporting_issues.consequence: Those studies were not read; their funders are unknown here.

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC9985244 (HTML): abstract, all sections of the main text, Tables 1 to 6, funding, competing-interest and affiliation statements; the reference list and the cited studies (Azzopardi 2021, Lee 2013, the in vitro and clinical papers) were not read
